pages.text: "Yum, yum! Time to eat!" Big sister Dodo ran from muddy play into the kitchen. Her muddy wings grabbed steaming bread. "Dodo, what about your wings?" little brother Mumu asked. She pretended not to hear.
"I know! Ducks live in water, so we're always clean!" Dodo munched. "I'll eat fast, then play in mud again!" Muddy wingprints marked the bread, with tiny wigglers hopping above them.

A little later, grumble went Dodo's tummy. It ached. "Oh, my tummy..." With drops at her eye corners, she sat on the floor and crossed both wings over her belly. Mom from the mill lowered her neck and laid a wing on Dodo's back. "It's okay. I'll take a look."

Dodo stretched both wings forward. Mom's beak pointed between the feathers. "Wigglers hid in the dry mud, then went in with the bread." "What do I do?" Mom turned toward the stream. "To the stream bank!"
At the shallow stream edge, Mom said, "Three steps for washing wings! One—dip them in the stream!" Dodo dipped both wings with a splash. Round ripples spread from the spot.
"Two—rub both wings together!" Mom showed her. Dodo rubbed too. Mud loosened, clouding the water, with little bubbling drops. Dodo called, "Wings scrubbed clean!"
"Three—preen between the feathers with your beak!" Mom carefully preened her own wing. Dodo followed, and the wigglers floated away. "Goodbye, wigglers!" Dodo grinned.
Dodo shook her wings in the sun. Dry and sparkling! Her sore tummy was fine now too. "Clean wings mean no tummy ache!" She flicked her tail once.
At snack time the next day, Dodo called before taking bread. "Wings first, before eating!" One, dip. Two, rub. Three, preen with the beak. Two clean wingprints stood side by side on the bread.

Mom hugged Dodo against her chest with both wings. "Our Dodo, the wing-washing champion!" Wash wings before eating, and your tummy feels good and bread tastes better. Dodo called, "Wings scrubbed clean! Mumu, let's eat together!"
